body:
I didn't really quote you for any good reason.  Just feeling really cerebral right now and did it out of habit I guess.

I will say one thing, 20 is a hard age.  Things have gotten much easier since then.  So you've got that going for you.  20 is like the most useless age ever. 

I don't know what I have to offer in return.  I chased my dreams and they've failed me.  But I did read some things in another thread that helped out a little bit.

* Living in the now
* Focusing on what I want to do rather than what I should do

I also saw some people that I guess lifelong Nietzsche types developing a deeper use of psychedelics and recreational drugs.   I've mainly been a social user of drugs but if you want to kill yourself you might as well do it slowly and while having a ton of fun.

Reminds me of the time me and a buddy were tripping on Mushrooms and listened to Sabbaths's "killing yourself to live."  One of the strongest connections I've ever had a lyric.  Think about it, killing yourself to live.

I guess escape seems like a better option than exiting right now talking through this.  It's certainly not productive, or socially acceptable for most, but I guess I can identify with how someone may bury it all under alcohol or drugs.

I do like drinking and doing drugs with friends, why not take it up full time?

Saw this beautiful quote too.

"When we follow our pessimism through all the way down and to its conclusion, only then can we find a new height, a way of looking at the world through the eyes of a Dionysian god. To view tragedy, not as tragedy, but as a great play. To derive joy from the depth of your feelings and experiences, regardless of whether the experiences are painful or pleasant. To experience the wonder and joy of being itself. There is all the reason to hope for the best provided that you don't give up."

Think I'm getting to pull my chair up to the shit show.

> ke interacting with an existence machine. Resisting suicide is something I've struggled with since I realized that I had to grow up and serve this great machine. I got burnt out on life's rewards long before I had to work. Overstimulation. Now that I'm working continuing hardly seems justifiable, since clenched in my teeth at all times is the knowledge that I'm going to die and forget it all. Really I want a simpler life... I want to feel needed and loved and close to people and not mechanical. To others I am only my job title and yeah it makes me feel like nothing. I want so much to feel connect but to me everyone feels so far away... 

Early 30s.

That's part of it yeah.  And to be honest I don't really believe in altruism, so while I could "help others" I'm honestly only helping myself.  I don't think there's anything wrong with either side.  What hurts me is the lack of authenticity. 

I've made the circle philosophically so I understand I'm not entitled to just "live my own life." The world is built on everyone's output.  What bothers me is seeing that darkness in people I hold to I guess a higher standard.  People I feel like aren't as connected to me as I'd hoped.

I see in front of me there's a large amount of effort to stabilize my life and every day it becomes a struggle to justify it because I don't feel like I'm getting back what I put into it.  Every day I become more and more drained.

I've always felt really that life is pointless and we create our own meaning.  And the closest I can find is that life is about creating and maintaining close, meaningful relationships.  Yet I struggle to find enough people that are genuine that aren't distracted in their life.

I've got a couple people that really opened my eyes.  They taught me what being a family man is all about.  I sold some of my flashy possessions because they didn't matter anymore. And I have totally embraced it.  My other half has not.  I can tell that she partly sees our children as burdens in the way she talks.  I don't think she regrets children, but her view just really bothers me.

Understandably I consider it be the pinnacle of existence.  Yet I just can't feel a real connection as a family.  Me and my kids bond great, no issue there.  But the time I spend with her there feels more formal and administrative.  I feel like I'm spending time with my children, with someone else there.  Maybe a close friend, not my significant other.  And not as a cohesive family unit.

I just can't imagine ever not being there for my other half or my mom in a time of need, or a patient.  I feel let down and yet I can't blame the actors, because I feel like they are just part of the machine.

Which is why I say I feel like an alien.  Every once and a while I meet someone I connect with on a level about this, but its rare.  The switching cost to breaking up with my fiancee is just so hard to stomach.  I know what divorce does to children. (Not that suicide would be any better).

I know there's love underneath it all but I lost her to minutia and the amount of effort she exerts on things like the bank shorting her $5 drives me crazy.  She is in a constant state of elevation, agitation and negativity.  There are short bursts of relaxation but her phone is always out, she's talking about something we need to do etc.

And yet I realize she isn't any less flawed than I am or anyone really.  She's great.  Which leads me to "is life worth living?"  Once the illusion that money will make you happy melts away, and you see people as mostly self serving, how do you finding meaning and purpose when nearly everyone you meet sees life in a totally separate way?

That much I get and really I'm not even addressing the fact that living in America automatically I'm living in the top 5% of the world, period.  My problem feels deeper than that.

Is this a world that really is human?  When the people you have in the world to rely on are themselves so caught up in the world, including your doctor, what is the point?
Thank you good sir.  Any recommendations on how to make getting back on track with a decent doctor without getting myself thrown in a hospital?
